title: —’Tis a custom more honoured in the breach than in the observance.
html_source:
A reference to Hamlet, Act I, Scene 4 line 18 in the Folger edition. Hamlet is telling Horatio about a Danish tradition where a musical flourish sounds when the king finishes a glass of wine. Hamlet says that this has led to the Danes having a regrettable reputation for drunkenness.

The sense here in both Ulysses and Hamlet is that, although “traditional”, it would be better if the act in question were no longer done.
